topicName: Jetpack Navigation Component and Deep Linking
content:
[{"order":1,"type":"heading","text":"Jetpack Navigation Component and Deep Linking in Android Kotlin"},{"order":2,"type":"paragraph","text":"The Jetpack Navigation component simplifies implementing navigation in your Android application. Combined with deep linking, it allows you to direct users directly to specific destinations within your app from external sources like notifications, web links, or shortcuts."},{"order":3,"type":"subheading","text":"1. Setting Up Dependencies"},{"order":4,"type":"paragraph","text":"First, add the required dependencies for the Navigation component in your app-level build.gradle.kts file."},{"order":5,"type":"code","text":"val navVersion = "2.7.7"
implementation("androidx.navigation:navigation-fragment-ktx:$navVersion")
implementation("androidx.navigation:navigation-ui-ktx:$navVersion")"},{"order":6,"type":"subheading","text":"2. Defining Deep Links in the Navigation Graph"},{"order":7,"type":"paragraph","text":"To enable deep linking to a specific destination, you must add a deepLink element to your navigation graph XML file. You can define explicit URI patterns and action types."},{"order":8,"type":"code","text":"<fragment
    android:id="@+id/detailFragment"
    android:name="com.example.app.DetailFragment"
    android:label="Detail">
    <argument
        android:name="itemId"
        app:argType="string" />
    <deepLink
        app:uri="https://www.example.com/item/{itemId}" />
</fragment>"},{"order":9,"type":"subheading","text":"3. Enabling Deep Links in AndroidManifest.xml"},{"order":10,"type":"paragraph","text":"You must inform the Android system about your navigation graph by adding the nav-graph element inside your activity's intent filter or relying on the Navigation host to handle deep links automatically."},{"order":11,"type":"code","text":"<activity
    android:name=".MainActivity"
    android:exported="true">
    <nav-graph android:value="@navigation/nav_graph" />
    <intent-filter>
        <action android:name="android.intent.action.VIEW" />
        <category android:name="android.intent.category.DEFAULT" />
        <category android:name="android.intent.category.BROWSABLE" />
        <data
            android:scheme="https"
            android:host="www.example.com"
            android:pathPrefix="/item" />
    </intent-filter>
</activity>"},{"order":12,"type":"subheading","text":"4. Handling Deep Link Arguments in Kotlin"},{"order":13,"type":"paragraph","text":"Inside your destination fragment, you can retrieve the arguments passed via the deep link using Safe Args or standard Bundle extraction."},{"order":14,"type":"code","text":"class DetailFragment : Fragment() {
    private val args: DetailFragmentArgs by navArgs()

    override fun onViewCreated(view: View, savedInstanceState: Bundle?) {
        super.onViewCreated(view, savedInstanceState)
        val itemId = args.itemId
        // Use the itemId to fetch and display data
    }
}"},{"order":15,"type":"subheading","text":"Best Practices"},{"order":16,"type":"bullet_point","text":"Always test your deep links via ADB using the command: adb shell am start -W -a android.intent.action.VIEW -d "https://www.example.com/item/123" com.example.app"},{"order":17,"type":"bullet_point","text":"Use Safe Args to ensure type safety when passing arguments between destinations and handling deep link extras."},{"order":18,"type":"bullet_point","text":"Keep your URI schemes distinct to prevent intent collision with other installed applications."}]
